info.title: Hopscotch
info.description:
An OpenAI-compatible inference API. Point an OpenAI client at https://api.hopscotchlabs.ai, give it a Hopscotch API key, and call models across providers on one prepaid balance.

Every response, errors included, matches the shape an unmodified OpenAI SDK expects.

customerApiKey.description: A workspace API key in an `Authorization: Bearer` header. A missing header, a scheme other than Bearer, a key of the wrong shape, and a key we reject are all 401.

Error.description: The error envelope. One top-level `error` key, always, at every status.

message.description: Prose for a person. It may be reworded, so do not branch on it.

type.description: The category an SDK branches on. A closed set.

param.description: The request field at fault, or null. Present and null rather than absent.

code.description: The stable machine-readable reason. Branch on this.

request_id.description: Our id for this request, the same value as the x-hopscotch-request-id header. Quote it when you contact support.

ChatCompletionRequest.description: An OpenAI chat completion request. Fields beyond the ones named here are forwarded to the provider unchanged rather than refused for being unfamiliar.

model.description: A model id in `family/model` form. List what you can call with GET /v1/models.

messages.description: The conversation so far, in OpenAI message form.

stream.description: Return the reply as server-sent events instead of one JSON body.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens you will accept. Sending it also lowers the credit held for the request while it runs, so it is the lever that keeps a request under your account spend rate cap. Omit it and the model's published maximum output is held instead.

stream_options.description: OpenAI stream options. Set `include_usage` to receive OpenAI's own usage chunk in the stream. Hopscotch's own counts arrive separately on the :x-hopscotch-usage comment line either way.

ChatCompletion.description: An OpenAI chat completion, as the provider produced it.

TextCompletion.description: An OpenAI text completion, as the provider produced it.

EmbeddingList.description: An OpenAI embedding list, as the provider produced it.

embedding.description: An array of numbers for `float`, or a base64 string for `base64`.

Message.description: An Anthropic message, as the provider produced it.

UsageRecord.description: One request, as the key that made it can read it back.

request_id.description: The id the `x-hopscotch-request-id` header carried on the response this record is about.

occurred_at.description: When the request started, in RFC 3339.

model.description: The full `provider/model` id the request was served under, the same string GET /v1/models publishes.

outcome.description: How the request ended, from a closed set of words. A request that was answered is `served`.

usage.description: Every count a charge can turn on. Null means the provider did not report that count. 0 means it reported none. They are not the same fact.

cache_write_tokens.description: The cache write at the default lifetime. It does not include `cache_write_1h_tokens`, so add the two to read the whole write.

cache_write_1h_tokens.description: The one-hour part of the cache write. Null where the provider stated no split.

charge.description: What the request cost, with what you need to check it against the rates GET /v1/models publishes. Present only when your workspace balance paid for the request, so it is absent when `paid_from_allowance` is true.

amount_micros.description: The charge in millionths of one dollar, so 1000000 is $1.00. Null where the request was never priced, which is not the same as a charge of zero.

amount.description: The same figure as dollars a person reads, with up to six decimal places and trailing zeros trimmed. Null exactly when `amount_micros` is null.

rate_revision_id.description: An opaque id for the set of rates this charge was computed from. Two requests with the same value were priced by the same rates. Null on a record written before rate revisions existed, or one left unpriced.

note.description: What was unusual about this charge, or null on an ordinary one. `rate_absent_charged_at_anchor`: part of the request was priced at a rate the model does not list, a cache read or write at the input rate or reasoning at the output rate. `estimated_from_delivered_text`: the stream stopped before the provider reported its counts, so the charge is the prompt we counted plus an output estimated from the text delivered, never above the amount held. `exact_from_provider_frame`: the stream stopped early but the provider counts had already arrived, so the charge is exact.

served_on_own_key.description: True when the request ran on your own provider key, which is why nothing was charged. Read this rather than inferring it from a zero charge.

paid_from_allowance.description: True when an included allowance paid for the request, in which case `charge` is absent.

latency_ms.description: Total time the caller waited, in milliseconds.

note.description: A fixed sentence saying no prompt and no response body was stored.

created.description: A unix timestamp in seconds. The release time where one is recorded and the record's own creation time otherwise, so it is not a release date for most of the list.

shutdown_date.description: When the model stops serving, in unix seconds. Absent when there is none, rather than null.

CatalogCapabilities.description: What the catalog records this model can do. Each answer is one of three words, and `unknown` is not `no`: it means nobody has established the answer.

ModelExtension.description: Our own facts about a model, under the `uniblock` key, which keeps the platform's original name because it is protocol a deployed client reads. Everything OpenAI's own model object defines stays at the top level; everything it does not define lives here.

model_id.description: The same value as `id`, repeated inside the extension so a client reading only this block still has it.

author.description: Who made the model, which is not who serves it.

input_rate_thousandths.description: The provider's own list price for prompt tokens, in thousandths of the currency unit per million tokens. Nothing this platform charges on top is folded in: the fee is taken when credit is bought, and a request then costs the provider's price.

output_rate_thousandths.description: The same unit, for completion tokens. Absent when the model publishes no separate output rate.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217, or null where nobody recorded one.

endpoint_families.description: The request families this model answers.

provider_display_names.description: Who can serve it. Which one answered a given request is on the response headers, not here.

ModelParameter.description: One request parameter this model accepts. The three bounds are in thousandths of the parameter's own unit, so a temperature ceiling of 2 arrives as 2000 and a default of 0.7 as 700. Integers, because a bound that drifted in its last decimal place would be a contract about nothing.

type.description: The control shape a client should render.

sent_by_default.description: Whether a client sends this parameter unless it is told otherwise.

ModelDetailExtension.description: Everything the list carries for a model, plus the five fields served only when one model is asked for by name.

description.description: Detail only. The list is scanned and the detail is read, so the prose a model carries is served where somebody asked for that one model.

replacement_model_id.description: What to move to, where one is named.

ModelDetail.description: One model, in the same envelope the list uses, with the detail-only fields under `uniblock`.

shutdown_date.description: Absent when the model has no announced end.

RequestId.description: Our id for this request. Quote it when you contact support. Present on every response, errors included.

SdkRequestId.description: The same value as x-hopscotch-request-id, on the header the official OpenAI SDKs surface on their error objects.

RetryAttemptCount.description: How many attempts were made before the response you received.

CacheStatus.description: Whether the reply came from cache.

TraceId.description: A trace id for this request.

ServedBy.description: The full id, "{provider}/{model}", of the model that actually answered: the id you pinned, or the member of the routing profile that served. Present on every served reply, streamed or not, which is the only place a streamed request can read it.

ServedVia.description: Present, with the value `backup`, when a backup route served this request. Absent on every other response, and never sent with any other value, so a client that has never read it sees nothing change about an ordinary request. The provider named on x-hopscotch-provider and in the body is still the one you asked for.

post.description:
Send an OpenAI chat completion request. Set `stream: true` for server-sent events.

Credit is held when the request is admitted and settled against the provider's own token counts when it finishes. You are charged the provider's rate at face value. Nothing is added per request.

model.description: The model to call, which the live catalog has to offer for the responses family. A provider-pinned id, `{provider}/{that provider's own id}`, is split once on the first slash. A routing-profile slug, `profile/{identifier}`, tries that profile's models in your own order. `unirouter/auto`, or its second spelling `hopscotch/auto`, names whichever route your workspace made its default. A bare model id is refused with 400 and the code `model_id_not_pinned`. `GET /v1/models` lists the exact strings this key can call.

200.description:
The completion. A response that is not streamed carries the provider's token counts in its own `usage` object. Its `model` field echoes the slug you asked for rather than the provider's internal name, except in three cases that are returned as the provider sent them: a streamed reply, whose frames are passed through unchanged; a request naming a routing profile, which names a chain rather than one model; and a successful body carrying no string `model` field at all.

When `stream` is true the body is `text/event-stream` instead, and the counts arrive on a `:x-hopscotch-usage` comment line immediately before `data: [DONE]`; the server-sent events specification requires parsers to ignore comment lines, so an SDK never sees it.

x-hopscotch-served-via.description: Present, with the value `backup`, when a backup route served this request. Absent on every other response, and never sent with any other value, so a client that has never read it sees nothing change about an ordinary request. The provider named on x-hopscotch-provider and in the body is still the one you asked for.

400.description: The request cannot be served as sent. `code` is null for a missing parameter, with `param` naming it, `context_length_exceeded` for a request too large to price or serve in one call, and `provider_key_refused` when the request ran on your own key for a provider that rejected it or refused this particular call under it. On the platform's own provider keys this route also refuses, with `code` null and `param` naming the field and never its value, a field that buys something this platform cannot bill yet or keeps the conversation at the provider: a `service_tier` other than `auto`, `default` or `on_demand`, `web_search_options`, a hosted tool the provider charges for per call, audio in or out, a `cache_control` marker with a `1h` ttl, and `store: true`. A request served on your own provider key keeps every one of them. See Request parameters.

error.message: You must provide a model parameter naming the model to call. It is read to work out what the request could cost before it is sent.

context_length_exceeded.summary: Too large to serve in one call

error.message: This request is too large to price: it is estimated at 4000000 prompt tokens, which is beyond anything this platform can hold credit for. Send less in one call.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key was rejected

error.message: openai rejected your workspace's own openai key (401), so the credential itself was not accepted. Replace it on the Provider keys screen. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

401.description:
No key, a scheme other than Bearer, a key of the wrong shape, or a key we reject. An unknown key and a revoked key are answered with one identical message on purpose.

A key past its own expiry date is refused here too, with code `key_expired` and a message naming the date. It is checked before the per-minute rate limiter, so an expired key never consumes that allowance. Expired keys are not renewed: create a new one.

error.message: Incorrect API key provided.

402.description: The request will not be paid for, and nothing was charged. Code `insufficient_credit` is the workspace being out of credit, which stops every key on it. Code `key_limit_exceeded` is the sending key reaching its own credit limit, which leaves every other key in the workspace serving normally; it is refused before any credit is held, and the message names what that key has settled and holds inside its current window.

insufficient_credit.summary: The workspace is out of credit

error.message: This account has 54 minor units available and the request needs 55 held.

key_limit_exceeded.summary: This key is at its own limit

error.message: This key may spend $20.00 in its current window and has $18.40 settled and $1.70 held against that, so a request needing $0.30 more is refused. Nothing was charged for it and no credit was held. The limit belongs to this key alone, so other keys in the workspace are unaffected. This limit resets monthly on UTC calendar windows, so requests are admitted again when the window rolls. It can also be raised or removed on the Keys screen.

403.description: Refused for a setting the caller owns rather than anything about the model, and `code` names which. A key whose account staff have suspended is refused with code `account_suspended`, before any credit is held or any provider is called; contact support, because retrying will not change the answer.

error.message: This account is suspended, so it cannot send requests. Contact support. Request id REQUEST_ID.

404.description: The model cannot be served, and the two cases are told apart by `code`. `model_not_found` means the id is in no catalog at all, which is what a typo produces, so check the spelling or list what this key can call with `GET /v1/models`. `model_not_available` means the id is catalogued and is not being served right now, either on this endpoint or at all, so retrying later is worth more than changing the request. No provider was called either way.

model_not_found.summary: No model of that id exists

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" does not exist. Check the spelling, or list the models this key can call with GET /v1/models.

model_not_available.summary: Known to us, and not being served right now

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" is not currently available. It is known to this platform and is not being served right now, so retrying later is worth more than changing the request.

model_not_available_endpoint.summary: Live, and not offered on this endpoint

error.message: "MODEL_ID" is not offered on this endpoint: the catalog lists it for chat and not for embeddings.

409.description: Reserved for workload insights, which is not available yet. A request that does not name a workflow never receives it.

413.description: The request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts, so it was refused at the door. A body that declares its length is refused without a byte being read; one that declares none is read only as far as the ceiling and then abandoned. Nothing was parsed, no credit was held, no model was called and nothing was charged.

payload_too_large.summary: The request body is over the ceiling

error.message: This request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts. Nothing was read, no model was called and nothing was charged. Send fewer messages, a shorter prompt, or fewer inputs.

429.description: A limit refused the request. `rate_limit_exceeded` is this key's own request rate and carries `Retry-After`. `spend_rate_exceeded` is the account spend rate cap, which counts the credit held for requests rather than the credit they settle at; send `max_tokens` to hold less. `provider_key_refused` is your own key for a provider being over its limit there; it clears on its own and carries no `Retry-After`. `upstream_rate_limited` is the model's provider rate-limiting the call: nothing about the request is wrong, nothing is charged, and it carries `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Present on `rate_limit_exceeded` and on `upstream_rate_limited`.

error.message: Rate limit reached for this key. Try again in 12 seconds. Request id REQUEST_ID.

This account has already reserved 5000 minor units in the last 60 seconds, which is at its ceiling of 5000. Requests are admitted again within 60 seconds of the earliest reservation counted, with nothing to do in the meantime.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key is over its limit

error.message: openai refused this request as over its limits, on your workspace's own openai key. This is your account's limit at openai rather than ours. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

upstream_rate_limited.summary: The model's provider rate-limited the call

error.message: The provider serving this model is rate-limiting requests right now. Nothing was charged. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Quote the request id if you contact support.

529.description: The model's provider answered `529` rather than `429`. Carries the same `upstream_rate_limited` code as the 429 case, with `type` `api_error` as the status class requires: nothing about the request is wrong, nothing is charged, and it carries `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Present the same way as on the 429 `upstream_rate_limited`.

upstream_rate_limited.summary: The model's provider rate-limited the call, at 529

error.message: The provider serving this model is rate-limiting requests right now. Nothing was charged. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Quote the request id if you contact support.

500.description: A fault on our side. The request id is the one thing worth keeping.

error.message: The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that! Quote the request id if you contact support.

503.description: Ours rather than yours, and `code` names the condition. `paused_by_owner` clears only when somebody lifts the pause, so retrying on a timer will not help. `balance_unavailable` (we could not read the balance, so the request was refused rather than served unmetered), `model_not_priceable` and `model_pricing_unreadable` (a model we list could not be priced for this call) and `no_provider_configured` (we are not currently configured to serve this) all clear without you doing anything.

error.message: Every request on this account is paused, because somebody with access to it pressed Pause in the dashboard. Nothing was charged for this request and no credit was held for it. It is retryable, and it will be refused the same way until the pause is lifted, so retrying on a timer will not clear it. Requests start working again the moment the pause is lifted from the same control, with nothing else to do and nothing to re-create.

post.description:

The body is forwarded as you sent it, so a field this page does not name still reaches the provider, and the reply is the provider's text completion object.

Read back what one request recorded and what it cost. Send the value of the `x-hopscotch-request-id` header from the response you are asking about. The key that made the request can read it, with no dashboard session.

The record is written after the response is sent, so a read taken the instant a response lands can arrive first and answer 404. Read it again a moment later. A record made by another key, a record outside this key's workspace, and an id that never existed all answer with the same 404, so this route cannot be used to learn whether an id exists.

In `usage`, null means the provider did not report that count and 0 means it was measured as none. The two are different facts. `charge` is present only when your workspace balance paid for the request. `served_on_own_key` is true when the request ran on your own provider key, and `paid_from_allowance` is true when an included allowance paid for it, in which case `charge` is absent. No prompt and no response body is stored, so none is returned.

This route counts against the calling key's own request rate limit, like every other route.

post.description:
Send a request in the Anthropic Messages format. Set `stream: true` for Anthropic's own server-sent event stream.

The credential is read from either `Authorization: Bearer` or Anthropic's own `x-api-key` header, so an unmodified Anthropic SDK works whichever way it authenticates. If both headers are present they must carry the same key: two different keys are refused with 401 rather than one being chosen.

`max_tokens` is required by Anthropic and is passed through as you send it. It is not defaulted here, and a request that leaves it out is refused by the provider in the provider's own words. It is also the figure the credit held for the request is sized from. An `anthropic-version` header is not forwarded.

This route differs from Anthropic's own API in one way: a refusal comes back in the OpenAI error envelope that every other route here uses, so an Anthropic SDK reads the sentence from `error.message`. Only `POST /v1/messages` is served. `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` is not, and answers 404 with the code `endpoint_not_supported`.

Credit is held when the request is admitted and settled against the provider's own token counts when it finishes. You are charged the provider's rate at face value. Nothing is added per request.

To read back the tokens and charge of one request afterwards, send the value of the `x-hopscotch-request-id` response header to `GET /v1/usage/{id}`.

parameters.name: x-api-key
parameters.description: Your Hopscotch API key, as an alternative to `Authorization: Bearer`. If you send both, they must carry the same key.

schema.description: An Anthropic Messages request. Fields beyond the ones named here are forwarded to the provider unchanged, so Anthropic's own documentation describes them.

model.description: A model id in `provider/model` form, or `profile/{identifier}` for one of your workspace's routing profiles. A bare model id is refused with 400 and the code `model_id_not_pinned`. The catalog must list the model for messages. List what you can call with GET /v1/models.

messages.description: The conversation turns, in Anthropic message form.

max_tokens.description: The most output tokens you will accept. Required, and passed to the provider as sent. The provider owns the ceiling for the model you name.

system.description: A system prompt, as Anthropic's API takes it: a string or an array of content blocks.

stream.description: Return the reply as Anthropic's own event stream instead of one JSON body.

tool_choice.description: How the model may use the tools, in Anthropic's form.

200.description:
The message, in Anthropic's format as the provider produced it: a `content` array, a `stop_reason`, and a `usage` object with `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`.

When `stream` is true the body is `text/event-stream` instead, passed through in Anthropic's own event format.

x-hopscotch-served-via.description: Present, with the value `backup`, when a backup route served this request. Absent on every other response, and never sent with any other value, so a client that has never read it sees nothing change about an ordinary request. The provider named on x-hopscotch-provider and in the body is still the one you asked for.

400.description:
The request cannot be served as sent. `code` is null for a missing parameter, with `param` naming it, `model_id_not_pinned` for a model id that names no provider, and `provider_key_refused` when the request ran on your own key for a provider that rejected it or refused this particular call under it. A refusal the provider made about this request, such as a missing `max_tokens`, is relayed with the provider's own status and its own sentence, quoted after the provider's name.

On the platform's own provider keys this route also refuses, with `code` null and `param` naming the field and never its value, a field that buys something this platform cannot bill yet: `container`, `mcp_servers`, a hosted tool the provider charges for per call, a one-hour cache write, and the priority, speed and regional processing fields. A request served on your own provider key keeps every one of them.

error.message: You must provide a model parameter naming the model to call. It is read to work out what the request could cost before it is sent.

model_id_not_pinned.summary: The model id does not name its provider

error.message: The model "gpt-4o-mini" does not name its provider. A model field carries either "provider/model", where the part before the first slash is a provider this platform serves and the rest is that provider's own id for the model, for example "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5", or "profile/{identifier}", one of your workspace's routing profiles, for example "profile/fast". GET /v1/models lists the exact strings this key can call.

max_tokens_missing.summary: The provider refused a request with no max_tokens

error.message: anthropic refused this request: max_tokens: Field required

mcp_servers.summary: A field this platform does not meter

error.message: "mcp_servers" asks the provider for something this platform does not meter yet (a priority or fast mode, regional processing, a hosted tool or search, audio, or a one-hour cache write). Remove it, or send the request on your own provider key.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key was rejected

error.message: openai rejected your workspace's own openai key (401), so the credential itself was not accepted. Replace it on the Provider keys screen. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

401.description: No key, a scheme other than Bearer with no `x-api-key` beside it, a key of the wrong shape, or a key we reject. An unknown key and a revoked key are answered with one identical message on purpose. Two different keys, one in `Authorization` and one in `x-api-key`, are refused too, with the same code and a message saying so. A key past its own expiry date is refused with code `key_expired` and a message naming the date.

error.message: Incorrect API key provided.
You did not provide an API key. Send it in an Authorization header using Bearer auth, or in x-api-key.
This request carried two different API keys, in Authorization and x-api-key. Send one credential.

402.description: The request will not be paid for, and nothing was charged. Code `insufficient_credit` is the workspace being out of credit, which stops every key on it. Code `key_limit_exceeded` is the sending key reaching its own credit limit, which leaves every other key in the workspace serving normally; it is refused before any credit is held, and the message names what that key has settled and holds inside its current window.

insufficient_credit.summary: The workspace is out of credit

error.message: This account has 54 minor units available and the request needs 55 held.

key_limit_exceeded.summary: This key is at its own limit

error.message: This key may spend $20.00 in its current window and has $18.40 settled and $1.70 held against that, so a request needing $0.30 more is refused. Nothing was charged for it and no credit was held. The limit belongs to this key alone, so other keys in the workspace are unaffected. This limit resets monthly on UTC calendar windows, so requests are admitted again when the window rolls. It can also be raised or removed on the Keys screen.

403.description: Refused for a setting the caller owns rather than anything about the model, and `code` names which. A key whose account staff have suspended is refused with code `account_suspended`, before any credit is held or any provider is called; contact support, because retrying will not change the answer.

error.message: This account is suspended, so it cannot send requests. Contact support. Request id REQUEST_ID.

404.description: The model cannot be served, and the two cases are told apart by `code`. `model_not_found` means the id is in no catalog at all, which is what a typo produces, so check the spelling or list what this key can call with `GET /v1/models`. `model_not_available` means the id is catalogued and is not being served right now, or that the catalog does not list it for this endpoint. In the second case the message names the endpoint families the catalog does list it for, so move to a model that is listed for this one. No provider was called either way.

model_not_found.summary: No model of that id exists

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" does not exist. Check the spelling, or list the models this key can call with GET /v1/models.

model_not_available.summary: Known to us, and not being served right now

error.message: The model "MODEL_ID" is not currently available. It is known to this platform and is not being served right now, so retrying later is worth more than changing the request.

model_not_available_endpoint.summary: Live, and not offered on this endpoint

error.message: "MODEL_ID" is not offered on this endpoint: the catalog lists it for chat_completions and not for messages.

405.description: A method other than POST on this path. The route boundary answers this before any key is looked at, so it costs nothing and reveals nothing.

error.message: GET is not supported for /v1/messages in this release.

409.description: Reserved for workload insights, which is not available yet. A request that does not name a workflow never receives it.

413.description: The request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts, so it was refused at the door. A body that declares its length is refused without a byte being read; one that declares none is read only as far as the ceiling and then abandoned. Nothing was parsed, no credit was held, no model was called and nothing was charged.

payload_too_large.summary: The request body is over the ceiling

error.message: This request body is larger than the 8388608 byte maximum this API accepts. Nothing was read, no model was called and nothing was charged. Send fewer messages, a shorter prompt, or fewer inputs.

429.description: A limit refused the request. `rate_limit_exceeded` is this key's own request rate and carries `Retry-After`. `spend_rate_exceeded` is the account spend rate cap, which counts the credit held for requests rather than the credit they settle at; send `max_tokens` to hold less. `provider_key_refused` is your own key for a provider being over its limit there; it clears on its own and carries no `Retry-After`. `upstream_rate_limited` is the model's provider rate-limiting the call: nothing about the request is wrong, nothing is charged, and it carries `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Present on `rate_limit_exceeded` and on `upstream_rate_limited`.

error.message: Rate limit reached for this key. Try again in 12 seconds. Request id REQUEST_ID.

This account has already reserved 5000 minor units in the last 60 seconds, which is at its ceiling of 5000. Requests are admitted again within 60 seconds of the earliest reservation counted, with nothing to do in the meantime.

provider_key_refused.summary: Your own provider key is over its limit

error.message: openai refused this request as over its limits, on your workspace's own openai key. This is your account's limit at openai rather than ours. While your workspace holds a key for openai, every request to openai runs on yours and none is sent on a Hopscotch key, so no other credential was tried for it. Nothing was charged for this request. Remove the key on the Provider keys screen and these requests go back to running on Hopscotch's key and being charged for.

upstream_rate_limited.summary: The model's provider rate-limited the call

error.message: The provider serving this model is rate-limiting requests right now. Nothing was charged. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Quote the request id if you contact support.

500.description: A fault on our side. The request id is the one thing worth keeping.

error.message: The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that! Quote the request id if you contact support.

503.description: Ours rather than yours, and `code` names the condition. `paused_by_owner` clears only when somebody lifts the pause, so retrying on a timer will not help. `balance_unavailable` (we could not read the balance, so the request was refused rather than served unmetered), `model_not_priceable` and `model_pricing_unreadable` (a model we list could not be priced for this call) and `no_provider_configured` (we are not currently configured to serve this) all clear without you doing anything.

error.message: Every request on this account is paused, because somebody with access to it pressed Pause in the dashboard. Nothing was charged for this request and no credit was held for it. It is retryable, and it will be refused the same way until the pause is lifted, so retrying on a timer will not clear it. Requests start working again the moment the pause is lifted from the same control, with nothing else to do and nothing to re-create.

balance_unavailable.summary: We could not read the balance

error.message: Your credit balance could not be checked while this request was running, so it was stopped rather than left unwatched. This is a fault on our side rather than a problem with your account, and it does not mean you are out of credit. Try again shortly.

504.description: The request ran past the request deadline and was terminated.

error.message: This request ran longer than the 540 second limit and was terminated. Reduce the amount of work in one call, or stream the response, and try again.
